topic: Middle Term and Applications of the Binomial Theorem
title: 1.01^1000 or 10000? Middle Term Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
1.01 is only a tiny bit more than 1. Multiply it by itself a thousand times: does it beat 10000? In this animated lesson on the binomial theorem (NCERT Chapter 7) we settle it without a calculator, then find the middle term of any expansion.

You will watch the terms of (1 + 0.01)^1000 add up live until the running total passes 10000, work through the NCERT example (1.01)^1000000 versus 10000, and see why two terms are enough. A row of cinema seats then shows when an expansion has one middle term and when it has two, and the hill of nCr shows why the middle term has the biggest coefficient. A worked example finds the middle term of (x + 2)^8, the exam trap catches the second middle term for odd n, and an original JEE Main pattern question closes the lesson with a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Note: comparing numbers with the binomial theorem is in the NCERT book. The middle term is not in the current (rationalised) NCERT text, but it is in the JEE Main syllabus.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
